name: Orthonectid Parasite of the Red Ribbon Worm

sections.overview: Intoshia linei is a minute marine orthonectid parasite whose host is the ribbon worm Lineus ruber.
sections.identification: The adult stage consists of short-lived, ciliated males and females with an extremely simplified body plan.
sections.habitat: Its parasitic plasmodia develop inside the tissues of Lineus ruber, a marine nemertean.
sections.diet: The free-living adults lack a digestive system; the trophic plasmodial stage lives within host tissues.
sections.behavior: When mature, males and females leave the host; observations show plasmodia can occupy several host tissues, including the nervous system.
sections.reproduction: The free-living sexes reproduce outside the host; comparative studies have examined how adults emerge.
sections.ecology: Its congener I. variabili parasitizes a flatworm rather than a nemertean, and researchers compare the two in studies of orthonectid genomes.
sections.conservation: The sources reviewed are parasitology and genome studies, not population surveys, and give no conservation category.
